title: Adrenal crisis
stem: Resus 2. Mr Lo, 45, has Addison's disease. He has had vomiting and diarrhoea for 2 days and couldn't keep his tablets down. He is confused and weak. HR 118, BP 78/44, RR 22, SpO2 97%, temperature 37.9 °C.

phases.title: Assess
phases.goal: Monitoring on, then assess him yourself: is this an adrenal crisis?

phases.title: Treat
phases.goal: Bloods only if they don't delay it: hydrocortisone, fluid and glucose from the cart, now.

phases.title: Ongoing plan
phases.goal: The next 24 hours and before he goes home.

events.say: He is drowsier and his pressure is falling: 68/40.
events.untreated: He deteriorated and never received hydrocortisone.

notes:
Checked against the Society for Endocrinology emergency guidance on adrenal crisis (2020/2023), NICE NG243 (Adrenal insufficiency, 2024) and the Endocrine Society guideline.

Adrenal crisis is a life-threatening emergency: hypotension/shock, vomiting, abdominal pain, confusion, often with hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia and hypoglycaemia. Do not wait for results: hydrocortisone 100 mg IV or IM immediately, then 200 mg over 24 hours (continuous infusion or 50 mg every 6 hours IV/IM); 0.9% saline 1 L over the first hour, then guided by response; check and treat glucose; treat the trigger (gastroenteritis, infection). Take a random cortisol and ACTH before steroid only if it does not delay treatment. Fludrocortisone is not needed while hydrocortisone is 50 mg or more per day. Afterwards: sick-day rules education, emergency card, injection kit.

Your notes list Addison's disease as a topic without detail.

opts.r: Far too little in crisis: 100 mg IV or IM now, then 200 mg over 24 hours.
Hydrocortisone provides glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid effect at stress doses.
Too slow for a BP of 78/44: 1 L over the first hour, then guided by response.
Too little to correct hypoglycaemia: 150–200 mL of 10% (15–20 g).
